sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.body_markdown: **Hold — unresolved; not a verified compounder or a current-price recommendation.** Methodhub is an acquisition-expanded IT consulting, staffing and managed-services group, with some telecom delivery and emerging product claims. Its useful customer relationships and signed work are real positives, but the software label does not establish a recurring platform moat. The decisive issue is converting attributable earnings into cash after acquired working capital, seller liabilities, expensive financing and minority interests. A verified current BSE price is unavailable, so ₹78.85 is an explicit scenario assumption, not the cutoff close. The conditional base can fund itself under stated rollover and collection assumptions, whereas a linked bear needs material equity rescue. Reconciled acquisition cash flows, stable organic customer economics and current liquidity evidence could change the conclusion. This is a potential cash-conversion/value or integration special situation, not a supported long-duration compounder designation. [E02–E08, E11, E13]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.body_markdown:
The group sells software implementation, cloud engineering, data/AI, cybersecurity, ERP, consulting and staff delivery, as well as telecom network implementation and managed services. Fixed-price engagements carry estimation and rework risk; time-and-material work depends on billable people, utilization, billing rates and collection. Contracts and repeat relationships can provide continuity without being subscription ARR. Geographic reach includes India, the US, Canada and Thailand; the latest precise external geography mix was not authenticated. Do not carry earlier customer/geography proportions into the expanded group. [E02–E04]

FY26 revenue comprises ₹311.5094 crore IT services, ₹18.4622 crore telecom and ₹2.9113 crore other operating revenue. Direct costs total ₹218.9754 crore, including consultant cost ₹105.9355 crore, cost of sales ₹96.8289 crore and material consumed ₹16.2110 crore. Inventory/WIP adjustments produce reported gross contribution ₹114.5432 crore before ₹31.5441 crore employee cost and ₹17.8957 crore other expenses. Therefore payroll alone seriously understates delivery labor. Core EBITDA excluding other income is ₹65.10 crore, or 19.56%. These are service/project margins, not proved software licence gross margins. [AR2026 pp 179–180]

The annual report lists 296 permanent employees; the July 500+professionals description may include contractors and expanded subsidiaries. The IPO gave 294 employees/consultants at 31 October 2025 versus 187 employees at FY25. FY25 attrition 5.78% compares with 5.92% in FY24 and 7.91% in FY23; H1 FY26's 5.74% is not annualized here. Onsite/offshore mix, billability, utilization, revenue per productive worker and pricing trends are unavailable. BalinX and QuantumHire require paid-customer and cost evidence before valuing them as products. [E02, E11]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.body_markdown:
A plausible advantage is embedded delivery knowledge, recruitment capability, customer familiarity and switching disruption during projects. SEW's exclusive MethodHub-branded sourcing arrangement and multi-year relationships can support repeat work. These are useful but contestable advantages: clients can in-source, renegotiate, shift vendors or reduce headcount. Non-solicitation terms during engagements and for a year afterward are not a durable network effect. No audited ARR, NRR, retention cohort or product unit economics demonstrates a proprietary platform moat. [E02–E03]

IPO FY25 top-one/top-five/top-ten concentration was 31.08%/70.41%/82.51%, while earlier-scope H1 FY26 was 32.09%/83.43%/91.95%. The largest customer, SEW, became 60%-owned. Consolidating a customer changes both gross revenue and eliminations; it does not eliminate dependence on that customer's end clients. Current external-client concentration is unknown. A strong rebuttal to the bear case would be independently disclosed renewals, stable gross profit per customer and cash realization after acquisition. [E03–E05]

Relevant prospectus peers are Esconet, InfoBeans and Silver Touch, but their hardware/infrastructure and software-service mixes differ. Issuer-selected FY25 revenues were ₹230.298/394.780/288 crore and EBITDA margins 4.38%/17%/13%. Their dated 20 November 2025 price/EPS pairs do not reproduce the printed multiples:182/6.11=29.79,566/15.58=36.33 and 830/22=37.73, not the table's 36.20/21.3/40.5. These are not current verified comparables and are not valuation anchors. No automatic SaaS premium is applied. [E14]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.body_markdown:
The accessible runway is existing clients buying more cloud, security, data and delivery support, plus proven contract renewals and cross-selling through acquired firms. The September Nemera award is approximately ₹161 crore over two years through July 2028. Dividing by two gives ₹80.5 crore annual gross contract capacity, not guaranteed incremental revenue. Parent ownership is 60% of SEW×51% of Nemera=30.6%; revenue consolidation and minority economic ownership are different. The model does not simply add the award to existing revenue because renewal, subcontracting and pass-through content are unverified. [E11]

A bottom-up scale path needs billable headcount × utilization × realized billing rate, plus recurring managed-service billings, less subcontractor costs and collection delays. Each term currently lacks a consistent new-scope history. A signed contract supports DUR6, but not a quantified high-CAP expansion. Approximately ₹31.94 crore software under development and ₹13.38 crore capital advances also show that the enlarged group is not financially capital-free. Product capitalization may be worthwhile or acquired; blanket expensing and blanket acceptance are both unsupported. [E02, E07]

SEW's disclosed standalone PAT ₹15.6022 crore ×60% less Leo's ₹3.4895 crore loss yields an indicative ₹5.87 crore owner-earnings contribution against ₹31.6443 crore equity purchase cost, or 18.56%. This is **not incremental ROIC**: the tables have differing period ends, debt and working capital are acquired, cash and intercompany eliminations are unreconciled, and step-down/NCI profits must not be double counted. Additional Nemera and S&R profit is not added to SEW/Leo without proving whether already included. [AR2026 pp 89–90,138,187]

Core NOPAT at an assumed 25% tax is ₹47.35 crore. Dividing by closing gross financed capital of ₹275.76 crore gives 17.17%; the average-capital proxy gives 26.93%. Neither establishes marginal organic returns, especially with acquisitions and the timing of the IPO. Goodwill is retained in capital; removing it to manufacture a high ROIC is inappropriate. A coherent stable-scope incremental NOPAT/capital bridge could support CAP without private project cohorts, but it is not presently available. GQS remains NS with 45% weighted coverage. [E05, E07–E08]

Foreign entities/partnership are outside CARO, and group IFC covers the holding company. sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.body_markdown:
**No current-price recommendation or ordinary entry range.** The authenticated cutoff price is missing. At the explicitly assumed ₹78.85, equity value is ₹148.66 crore and reported owner PATP/E is 4.67×. This inexpensive-looking diagnostic is not evidence of value until earnings/cash/ownership and execution are dependable. Removing other income and assuming five-year amortization of ₹31.9386 crore SUD at 25% tax and observed profit attribution produces illustrative owner PAT ₹26.91 crore and P/E5.53×. This is a normalization scenario, not an audited restatement or a claim all SUD was current R&D. [E05–E08, E10, E13]

The primary method is an attributable earnings multiple with a complete conditional cash/debt/share bridge. The terminal P/E applies to earnings after interest; debt is not subtracted again. Terminal free cash above ₹12 crore reserve is added once using an explicit parent profit/cash allocation proxy 81.64%; no interest income is included in earnings, and neither restricted cash nor operating assets get a second valuation. Entity cash access and future NCI mix make this an assumption, sensitized at 70%/observed/100%. No unsupported DCF precision or stale peer P/E is used.

The bear loses 50% of aged good AR and repays 25% of revolver, versus 10%/5% aged loss and no rollover cut in base/bull. An additional base case at 6×P/E tests multiple compression. No unpriced acquisition or incremental Nemera award is added on top.

The monthly schedule starts 31 March 2026, explicitly counterfactual through 20 October 2026, then ends exactly 20 October 2031. Each interval first prefunds interest, tax, capex, WC, claims and principal, then receives positive operating cash; no future cash cures an earlier breach. Maintenance capex starts ₹1.5 crore/year and grows 5%; product investment is 1% of revenue; growth fixed assets are 1% of incremental revenue run rate. Existing SUD is commissioned/amortized over five years as an assumption. Old purchase claims and tax/statutory dues are paid within year one, eligible IPO draws only against eligible uses; interest free principal is repaid March 2028 and other term principal is capped at ₹3.2379 crore. Recurring costs do not disappear when IPO money runs out. No terminal cash use is scheduled after the exit.

The first non-rescue bear funding gap arises before entry. Its terminal price is a diagnostic failed path, **not a valid return or entry price**. The distinct rescue scenario issues whole shares at ₹60 with 5% fees before the interval uses, including pre entry. It raises ₹51.08 crore gross, ₹48.53 crore net; final shares 27367297, share expansion 45.16%, old-holder dilution 31.11%. These are different measures. The conditional rescue IRR is-27.74%; no actual rescue is asserted.

Funded conditional 12%/15%/18% hurdle prices, all annual/monthly rows, June actual/model comparisons and 51 two-way sensitivity rows are in the model annex and canonical record. Surviving conditional base 15% hurdle price is ₹114.42, not a recommended entry. Two-way tests cover WC/rollover, growth/multiple, reserve/product capex, margin/finance cost, ownership/rescue price and net aged AR loss/incremental recourse calls. The reverse growth solver scans−25% to 60%, requires a finite funded bracket, and converges to 3.25% growth for 15% return under the base assumptions. It does not claim that the actual market implies that growth. Cash accumulation and assumed terminal normalization drive that result; changing funding/cash quality can invalidate it. Ordinary R, D, P and entry remain NS.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.body_markdown:
The strongest bear case is not that software consultants are intrinsically bad businesses. It is that acquisition accounting and expensive credit mask weak cash unit economics: a concentrated end customer delays payment, old receivables require write offs, discounted bill recourse is called, the factor trims funding, and payroll/sellers/taxes still fall due. The model links−8% revenue growth,10% cash margin,150 W Cdays,50% aged AR loss,21% finance cost and 25% revolver reduction. It breaches the analyst's ₹12 crore cash reserve before entry and requires ₹51.08 crore of assumed rescue equity. A later positive cash balance cannot validate an unfunded early path.

The old receivables and ₹23.1693 crore discounted bills are stressed as separate cash claims only to the extent not already reflected in debt; zero/50%/100% incremental recourse is crossed with 10%/50% loss on net aged AR and adverse tax ₹0.2315 crore. Large calls can fail otherwise profitable paths. There is no allegation those calls have occurred. Minimum reserve itself is tested at ₹6/12/18 crore so an analyst choice is not passed off as legal insolvency. [E07–E09]

Permanent loss can arise from unrecoverable acquired receivables, worthless development/goodwill, continued owner profit not converting to cash, financing costs absorbing gross profit, or repeated equity issuance at discounts. All are more serious than ordinary share-price volatility. Conversely, verified collection of the aged pool, clear cash/noncash seller reconciliation, refinancing on better terms and stable owner profit would weaken this bear case. The decisive falsification variable is **normalized attributable cash after working capital, interest and necessary reinvestment**, not reported revenue growth.

The appropriate classification is **Speculative / unsupported**, not a multibagger forecast. At the assumed ₹78.85, unchanged shares,10% owner PAT margin and no extra cash value, the following mechanical requirements apply:

| Price gain | Terminal P/E | Required owner PAT ₹cr | Required revenue ₹cr | Required revenue CAGR | Required price CAGR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5× | 6 | 123.88 | 1238.83 | 26.69% | 37.98% |
| 5× | 10 | 74.33 | 743.30 | 15.56% | 37.98% |
| 10× | 6 | 247.77 | 2477.65 | 43.53% | 58.50% |
| 10× | 10 | 148.66 | 1486.59 | 30.92% | 58.50% |

Revenue CAGR starts 31 March 2026 and ends 20 October 2031 (2029 days/365.25); investor price CAGR starts 20 October 2026 and ends 20 October 2031 (1826 days/365.25). These different denominators are intentional.

The decomposition is revenue growth×owner-margin change×old/new shares×P/Echange. Acquired gross revenue does not directly equal owner share growth. Rescue dilution raises the earnings requirement; lower multiples demand more profit. A large addressable IT market is not proof of accessible market share. No verified organic growth, retention, collection or incremental return history supports treating either outcome as probable. The bull model is illustrative, not evidence of execution.

sections.body_markdown:
**Hold — unresolved. Exclude from investable ranking. No verified compounder designation, ordinary expected return, entry range or position recommendation.** The scorecards remain NS because required organic-growth, incremental-return and price-dependent inputs are not supported. BQS/GQS missing-factor bounds describe uncertainty, not a ranking substitute. There is no mechanical downgrade because the business uses contractors or lacks tangible factories.

Reopen G2 after a consolidated acquisition opening-balance and cash/noncash bridge, including exact seller settlement, intragroup subscriptions, NCI and corrected CFO. Reopen G3 after dated available-cash, eligible IPO deployment, factoring/renewal and liability settlements form a coherent conservative funding bridge. A private daily bank statement is not inherently required if sufficient public evidence supports it. Reopen G4 with an authenticated BSE quote, dated 20/60-session liquidity, spread, lot and restrictions. Then re-run the model at the verified price and revisit R/D/P/L rather than carrying forward scenario scores. Low price alone does not resolve unreliable cash earnings.

summary: **Hold — unresolved; not a verified compounder or a current-price recommendation.** Methodhub is an acquisition-expanded IT consulting, staffing and managed-services group, with some telecom delivery and emerging product claims. Its useful customer relationships and signed work are real positives, but the software label does not establish a recurring platform moat. The decisive issue is converting attributable earnings into cash after acquired working capital, seller liabilities, expensive financing and minority interests. A verified current BSE price is unavailable, so ₹78.85 is an explicit scenario assumption, not the cutoff close. The conditional base can fund itself under stated rollover and collection assumptions, whereas a linked bear needs material equity rescue. Reconciled acquisition cash flows, stable organic customer economics and current liquidity evidence could change the conclusion. This is a potential cash-conversion/value or integration special situation, not a supported long-duration compounder designation. [E02–E08, E11, E13]
